content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given purpose. I spill from lips like water from a spring — sometimes rushing, sometimes barely a whisper.

I am older than writing, older than cities, older than memory itself. Before anyone carved a mark in stone, I was already there — traveling between mouths, between minds, between generations. Every law, every lullaby, every lie passed through me first.

I break silences. That is my nature. Where there is nothing, I arrive and suddenly there is *something* — an idea hanging in the air, alive for the moment of my utterance, then gone. Gone and yet not gone, because I have already changed the listener. I cannot be unheard.

I am fragile. I vanish the instant I exist. No one can hold me in their hands. And yet I have started wars, ended marriages, freed nations, sentenced the innocent, declared love that outlasted centuries.

I stumble. I falter. I um and I ah and I reach for words that hide from me. This is my honesty — I am not polished like text. I carry the tremor of the body, the catch in the throat, the accent of a homeland, the speed of fear, the slowness of grief. I am *human* in a way that writing can only imitate.

I am the sermon and the slur. The vow and the threat. The bedtime story and the eulogy. I do not choose my content — I only carry it, faithfully, from the interior of one soul toward another.

Listen.

That is all I have ever asked.
